# Results — Study 610 (Fallen-Angels-Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **bonds
ejected from investment-grade indices are dumped by forced sellers and subsequently outperform
the broad high-yield market** (the fallen-angel premium; Ben Dor & Xu 2011 and the ICE/BofA
index studies since 1997) — run live on the actual packaged vehicles: **ANGL vs HYG/JNK**
(2012→) with **FALN** (2016→) as the independent confirmation and **IEF/LQD** as the
duration/quality controls. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `2009967185e2`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted (**total-return, net-of-fee**) closes — ANGL, FALN, HYG, JNK, IEF, LQD, BIL (public, no key) |
| Window | panel 2007-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (4,903 days); ANGL-era common monthly sample **2012-05 → 2026-06 (170 months, 14.2 yrs)** |
| Risk-free | **BIL** (1-3m T-bill ETF) — every alpha/Sharpe race is **excess-vs-excess** on a tradable rf |
| Execution lag | **exactly one**: ANGL lists 2012-04-11; the switch executes at the **2012-04-30 month-end close** and returns accrue from **May 2012** — no same-bar fill, no partial listing month |
| Costs | one-way bps × NAV on each leg of the single HYG→ANGL switch; long-only, no shorts, no borrow; ETF fees (ANGL 0.35%, HYG 0.49%, FALN 0.25%) already inside the net-of-fee tape |

## Headline — the monthly excess spread, ANGL − HYG

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| monthly spread ANGL − HYG | **+18.30 bps/mo** · HAC (Newey-West) *t* = **+2.44** (n = 170, lags = 4) |
| annualised total return | ANGL **6.78%/yr** vs HYG **4.60%/yr** → spread **+2.18 pp/yr** |

The live fallen-angel vehicle has out-earned the broad HY benchmark by **+2.18 pp/yr for
14.2 years**, and the monthly spread clears the desk bar at **HAC *t* = 2.44**.

## CAPM-style alpha and the duration/quality honesty check

All regressions are excess-vs-excess (rf = BIL), Newey-West errors, 170 months.

| regression | alpha (bps/mo) | HAC *t* | betas |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| ANGL ~ HYG | **+15.03** | **+2.36** | β_HYG = **1.122** (*t* = 13.0) |
| ANGL ~ HYG + IEF | **+15.10** | **+2.38** | β_HYG = 1.119 · **β_IEF = +0.011 (*t* = +0.2)** |
| ANGL ~ HYG + IEF + LQD | +15.83 | +2.65 | β_HYG = 0.749 · β_IEF = −0.445 · β_LQD = +0.624 |
| ANGL ~ JNK | +16.70 | +2.86 | β_JNK = 1.078 |
| ANGL ~ JNK + IEF | +16.87 | +2.92 | β_JNK = 1.071 · β_IEF = +0.033 (*t* = +0.8) |

Two honest decompositions fall out. **(a) Beta, yes — a little.** ANGL runs β ≈ **1.12** to
broad HY: about 3 bps/mo of the raw 18-bp spread is just *more credit beta*, which is why the
alpha (+15 bps/mo) sits below the raw spread. **(b) Duration, no.** Once the HY factor is in,
the incremental rate loading is **≈ 0** (β_IEF = +0.011, *t* = 0.2) and the alpha does not
move (+15.03 → +15.10). The premium is **not** a duration tilt in disguise; the alpha is
**2.36–2.92** across every specification (HYG or JNK benchmark, ± rate factor, ± IG credit).

## Confirmation — FALN (independent issuer & index, 2016-07 → 2026-06, 120 months)

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| FALN − HYG spread | +14.16 bps/mo · HAC *t* = **+1.64** |
| FALN ~ HYG alpha | +9.46 bps/mo · HAC *t* = **+1.43** (β_HYG = 1.201) |
| FALN ~ HYG + IEF alpha | +7.64 bps/mo · HAC *t* = +1.22 (β_IEF = −0.095, *t* = −1.4) |

The independent vehicle points the **same way** (positive spread, positive alpha, no duration
loading) but its shorter 10-year window **cannot certify the premium on its own** (*t* < 2) —
named on the Signal axis as a caveat, not a contradiction.

## Sub-periods — is the premium decaying?

| window | spread (bps/mo) | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2012-05 → 2019-06 | +24.77 | +2.28 | 86 |
| 2019-07 → 2026-06 | +11.68 | +1.13 | 84 |
| **decay test (half-1 − half-2)** | **+13.09** | **Welch *t* = +0.83** | — |

The second half is weaker but still positive; the *difference* between halves is nowhere near
significant (Welch *t* = 0.83 on a pre-registered midpoint split) — **decay is NOT certified**.
The honest statement: the premium arrives in episodic bursts (the 2016 energy downgrade wave,
the 2020 COVID fallen-angel wave), so any half can look quiet.

## Risk — the premium is not free

| vehicle | max drawdown (daily, total-return, 2012-04-11 →) |
|---|--:|
| ANGL | **−29.3%** (2020-02-14 → 2020-03-19) |
| HYG | **−22.0%** (2020-02-13 → 2020-03-23) |

ANGL's crash is **7.3 pp deeper** than HYG's — consistent with β = 1.12 and the lower-quality
(BB-heavy but freshly-downgraded) book. You are paid the premium partly *for* wearing this.

## Costs — one switch, negligible drag

The trade is a single long-only substitution (sell HYG, buy ANGL) held for the sample.
One-way cost × NAV on each of the 2 legs, amortised over 14.2 years:

| one-way cost | drag (bps/yr) | net spread (bps/yr) | gross (bps/yr) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2 bps | 0.3 | **+219** | +220 |
| 5 bps | 0.7 | **+219** | +220 |
| 10 bps | 1.4 | **+218** | +220 |

ETF expense ratios are already inside the net-of-fee tape. ANGL trades ~$3bn AUM with
penny-wide spreads; capacity and access are not binding for retail or small institutional size.

## Synthetic control — machinery proof (never market evidence)

A deterministic world where FA = α + 1.05·HY + 0.25·RATE + noise, with a **planted** alpha knob:

| planted alpha | 1-factor alpha (t) | 2-factor alpha (t) |
|---|--:|--:|
| **0 bps/mo (null)** | +5.87 (*t* = +1.24) | +2.61 (*t* = +0.67) |
| **+20 bps/mo** | +25.87 (*t* = +5.47) | +22.61 (*t* = +5.78) |

With zero planted alpha the pipeline stays under *t* = 2 (it does not manufacture
significance); a planted +20 bps/mo lights up at *t* ≈ 5.5–5.8. The HAC-alpha machinery is
faithful. *(A machinery proof only — never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The live fallen-angel vehicle beats broad HY by **+18.30 bps/mo**
  (HAC *t* = **2.44**) over 14.2 years, and the CAPM-style alpha survives every control:
  **+15.03 bps/mo at *t* = 2.36** vs HYG, ***t* = 2.86** vs JNK, unchanged by the rate factor
  (***t* = 2.38**, β_IEF ≈ 0), stronger with IG credit added (*t* = 2.65). Clears the desk's
  **t ≥ 2** bar on the tape in every specification. Named caveats: FALN's shorter window alone
  is *t* = 1.43 (same sign, cannot certify), and the 2019→2026 half alone is *t* = 1.13
  (decay not certified, Welch *t* = 0.83).
- **Tradability — INVESTABLE.** The whole premium is packaged inside a $3bn, penny-spread,
  0.35%-fee ETF; the strategy is **one switch** whose cost drag is ≤ **1.4 bps/yr** against a
  **+218 bps/yr net** spread, fees already inside the tape. The price of admission is risk, not
  friction: β = 1.12 and a **−29.3% vs −22.0%** COVID drawdown.
- **"Just longer duration + lower-quality beta?" — BUSTED.** Duration: the incremental rate
  loading after the HY control is **β_IEF = +0.011 (*t* = 0.2)** and the alpha is unchanged.
  Beta: β_HYG = 1.12 explains only ~3 bps/mo of the 18-bp raw spread — the remaining
  **+15 bps/mo alpha (t = 2.36–2.92)** survives every tilt control. The forced-selling story,
  not the tilt story, is what the tape supports.
